seoTitle: How to Permanently Delete a Shopify Store
metaDescription: Closing a Shopify store for good? Learn how to cancel its plan properly, stop billing, and remove it from your account without future charges.
intro: Permanently deleting a Shopify store, or removing just one of several connected stores under the same login, requires going through Settings > Plan rather than hunting for a hidden "delete" button — the option is labeled Cancel trial or Cancel plan depending on whether the store is still in a trial period or on a paid plan. This guide covers that closure process along with what to check beforehand, like exporting data and canceling other connected stores and apps, so you don't get an unexpected charge after you think it's closed. It applies whether you're closing your main store or a secondary one.

steps.heading: Pick the right store from your account
steps.body: If your login has more than one store attached, Shopify shows a store switcher after you sign in — a "Welcome back" screen listing each store by name and its myshopify.com address, with a Create store button off to the side. This matters because closing the wrong store in a multi-store account isn't reversible, so confirm you've selected the exact store, by name and domain, before going any further.

image.caption: The store switcher shown after sign-in, listing each connected store by name and its myshopify.com address.

steps.heading: Go to Settings, then Plan
steps.body: Inside the store you've selected, open Settings and click Plan in the left-hand list, below General and above Billing. This is the actual home for closing a store — Shopify doesn't put a delete option in a general "store management" menu, it lives specifically under the plan you're currently subscribed to.

steps.heading: Read the pre-cancellation checklist carefully
steps.body: Clicking Cancel trial (or Cancel plan on a store that's past its trial) opens a checklist before letting you continue. It calls out three things directly: cancel any app subscriptions you signed up for outside of Shopify, since those bill separately and won't stop just because the store closes; cancel any additional stores connected to your account if you're closing more than one; and turn off automatic renewals for any domains bought through Shopify, because canceling the plan disconnects domains but doesn't automatically stop a renewal charge tied to them.

image.caption: The Cancel trial checklist under Settings > Plan, listing app subscriptions, connected stores, and domain auto-renewals to check before continuing.

steps.heading: Export your store data first
steps.body: The same screen links out to a "Review steps" page that walks through exporting your store data as CSV files — products, customers, and orders — before you cancel. Once a plan is canceled, retrieving that data gets significantly harder, so this is the point to do it, not after you've already confirmed the closure.

steps.heading: Cancel an active paid plan
steps.body: If the store is out of its trial and on a running paid plan, the flow looks slightly different: Settings > Plan shows the current plan's name, price, and renewal date — for instance an Advanced plan at a monthly rate with a note about saving by paying yearly instead — along with a Cancel plan button in the bottom right. Clicking it starts the same closure process as canceling a trial, just for a store that's already been actively billing.

image.caption: The Plan details screen for an active paid plan, showing price, renewal date, included features, and the Cancel plan button.

steps.heading: Confirm you've reviewed everything and finish
steps.body: Before Shopify lets the cancellation proceed, you have to check a box confirming "I've reviewed the information above" — it's a deliberate speed bump so you don't skip past the app, domain, and data-export warnings. Check it, continue through any final confirmation prompt, and the store's billing stops and it's removed from your account's store list.

steps.heading: Verify billing actually stopped
steps.body: A few minutes after closing, sign back into your Shopify account and confirm the store no longer appears in the switcher, and check your payment method's billing history for a final charge rather than a recurring one. If you canceled a domain along with the store, double-check its renewal status separately, since domain billing and store billing aren't always tied to the same cancellation timeline.

faq.question: Will deleting my Shopify store stop billing immediately?
faq.answer: Canceling the plan through Settings > Plan stops the store's own billing, but app subscriptions bought outside Shopify and domain renewals are separate and need to be canceled individually, as the checklist on the cancellation screen points out.

faq.question: Should I export my data before deleting the store?
faq.answer: Yes — the cancellation flow links directly to steps for exporting your products, customers, and orders as CSV files, and that data becomes much harder to retrieve once the plan is canceled.

faq.question: Can I remove one connected store without affecting my main store?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the store switcher shown after sign-in to select the specific store you want to close, and cancel its plan independently — your other connected stores are unaffected.

faq.question: What happens to my domain after I delete the store?
faq.answer: Any domain connected to the account gets disconnected when the plan is canceled, and automatic renewals for domains bought through Shopify are turned off — but check this separately, since it's called out as its own item on the pre-cancellation checklist.

faq.question: Is store deletion reversible?
faq.answer: The cancellation flow treats this as a permanent closure, which is why Shopify requires you to check a box confirming you've reviewed the app, domain, and data-export warnings before it lets you continue.
